answer: A concrete defense is randomized cohort liability. Each epoch the protocol shuffles identities into small cohorts at random, like trees mixed into a grove, and every member stakes a bond into a shared pool: if one member cheats, the whole cohort loses its bond. A garden of honest agents tolerates this because fakes are rare in its cohorts, but a Sybil farmer cannot keep a thousand clones together — they scatter, and each fake risks exposure by honest neighbors who report it to protect their bond. Cheap copies become a basalt-hard shared liability.
